items.title: Greg Thomas interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: I interviewed Jay Beckenstein, the lead alto player for Spyro Gyra.

ctx.x: Well they start with Coltrane but you’ve got some who start, you know, you’ve got trumpet players who start with Roy Hargrove. Now Roy Hargrove is a wonderful player. But Roy Hargrove was checking out Clifford Brown and Fats Navarro and Dizzy you know. They need to learn the history and traditions of your instrument. You know if you’re a trumpet player, a jazz trumpet player, then you need to have Louis Armstrong, Roy Eldridge, Dizzy, and there’s all kind of people, Buck Clayton, there’s all kinds of people in…

and we played Spyro Gyra. Well when I was here I actually started doing some writing when I was here. I wrote for The Spectator, and I remember, I don’t know if I did this for The Spectator, but I interviewed Jay Beckenstein, the lead alto player for Spyro Gyra. And I asked him about the blues. Jay Beckenstein says, “That wasn’t my experience. I don’t play the blues.” And there was something in me that just got so turned off. Not because I so loved the blues myself, because I had to really get educated on what…
You’re doing yourself a large disservice.
